n: Zephaniah calls the shameless nation of Judah to gather together — to assemble in repentance while there’s still time.

f.g: In Hebrew, a play on gathering straw or stubble — they are like chaff.

n: Do it before the decree takes effect, before the day blows away like chaff, before the Lord’s fierce anger arrives.

f.g: The husks blown away when grain is winnowed.

n: Seek the Lord, all you humble people who keep His commands. Seek righteousness and humility — perhaps you will be hidden on the day of His anger. Zephaniah’s name (“the Lord hides”) is echoed here.

f.w: Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth
it may be ye shall be hid

n: Now judgment turns to the nations, starting west with the Philistine cities. In Hebrew there are puns: Gaza (Azzah) will be abandoned (azubah), and Ekron uprooted (te‘aqer).
Woe to the coastal people, the Cherethites (Philistines from Crete). God will destroy Philistia completely.

f.g: A Philistine group, likely originally from Crete.

f.w: O Canaan, the land of the Philistines

n: The coast will become pastureland, with shepherds’ huts and sheep pens.
That coastland will belong to Judah’s faithful remnant. The Lord will care for them and restore their fortunes.

f.g: Restore their fortunes; bring back the exiles.

n: Turning east: God has heard Moab and Ammon mocking His people and boasting against their borders.
God swears Moab and Ammon will become like Sodom and Gomorrah — weeds and salt pits forever. Fittingly, both nations descended from Lot, who escaped Sodom.

f.g: Salt flats near the Dead Sea — barren land.

n: This is what pride earns: they mocked and bragged against the Lord’s people.

f.w: This shall they have for their pride

n: The Lord will make all the false gods waste away, and people everywhere — even in distant coastlands — will worship Him.

f.w: famish all the gods of the earth
f.g: Starve them — idols will lose their worshipers and offerings.

f.w: all the isles of the heathen

n: To the far south: Ethiopia (Cush) too will fall by God’s sword.

f.g: Cushites, from the Nile region south of Egypt; Cushite kings had ruled Egypt.

n: To the north: God will destroy Assyria and make Nineveh a dry wasteland. Nineveh fell in 612 BC.
Wild animals and birds will roost in Nineveh’s ruins; their calls will echo through empty windows. Its fine cedar paneling will be exposed to the weather.

f.g: A wild bird — perhaps the desert owl.
Perhaps the hedgehog or a screech owl.

n: This was the proud city that felt secure and said, “I am, and there is no one else.” Now it is a den for animals, and passersby hiss and shake their fists.

f.w: I am, and there is none beside me
